paper.title: Best Arm Identification Based Beam Acquisition in Stationary and Abruptly Changing Environments

settings.name_in_paper: Stationary environment problem P1 with concurrent beam-group probing (CBE)
unmapped: Learner may activate a group of N/2 beams simultaneously and observe one Gaussian sample whose mean/variance is the (power-scaled) sum over the group (concurrent multi-beam probing)
Gaussian rewards with variance proportional to mean: sigma_i^2 = 2 sigma^2 mu_i
Best beam has gain G, all others gain g (two-level means); highly directional orthogonal beams with negligible cross terms
The detection threshold uses g, G and sigma, so the learner knows these

settings.name_in_paper: Stationary best beam identification (no change) with Sequential Halving
unmapped: Gaussian rewards with variance proportional to mean: sigma_i^2 = 2 sigma^2 mu_i
settings.definition_quote: In case of no change, the performance of \texttt{SH} is exponentially bounded as $\log N \exp\left(-\frac{1}{2}\frac{\Delta^2_{\min}T}{N\log N }\right)$, which is of the form given in~\cite{karnin2013almost}.

settings.name_in_paper: Abruptly changing environment problem P2 (single abrupt change making a suboptimal beam optimal)
unmapped: Exactly one change: a single suboptimal beam's mean jumps at random time t_c and becomes optimal; target is the best arm at time T
Change time is random with a distribution F (bounds depend on it)
The changing beam is among the top K_c beams; K-SHES knows K_c
Gaussian rewards with variance proportional to mean
settings.definition_quote:
\begin{align}
    {\rm P}_2:\qquad& \argmax_i \mu_i(T), \nonumber \\
    {\rm st} \qquad&  R(t) \sim \mathcal{N}\left(\mu_i(t), \sigma_i(t)\right), \quad \forall i, \forall t \in [T] \nonumber \\
    &\mu_i(t) = \mu_i, \quad \forall i\neq j, \forall t, \nonumber \\
    &\mu_j(t) = \mu_j^-, \quad  0 \leq t \leq t_{\rm c}, \nonumber \\
    &\mu_j(t) = \mu_j^+, \quad  t_{\rm c} < t \leq T, \nonumber \\
   {\rm within} \qquad& T. \nonumber 
\end{align}

symbols.L_1: max{C_1, C_2}, constants that vanish as sidelobe gain g -> 0
symbols.sigma_n: noise parameter sigma with arm variance sigma_i^2 = 2 sigma^2 mu_i

conditions: highly directional orthogonal beams (cross terms neglected)
best beam gain G, all other beams gain g
noise variance much smaller than transmit power
tuning: log N rounds, one per beam group, LLR threshold gamma
results.notes: Paper's N = number of beams = K; logs are base 2. Quantity is probability of misidentifying the best beam. Proof is heuristic.

source.quote: In case of no change, the performance of SH is exponentially bounded as \log N \exp(-\frac{1}{2}\frac{\Delta^2_{\min}T}{N\log N }), which is of the form given in~\cite{karnin2013almost}.

results.notes: Variance dependence not shown in the stated expression; logs base 2.

bound.regime: conditioned on change in the first r* = log(N/(2K)) + 1 rounds

symbols.K_c: rank (K-th best) of the beam that undergoes the change

conditions: single abrupt change in the K_c-th best beam making it optimal

source.label: lem:ec
source.quote: Conditioned on the change occurring within the first r^* = \log \frac{N}{2K} + 1 rounds, the probability that the best arm is eliminated is upper bounded as P^{SH}_C(T | r_c \leq r^*) \leq 2 (\log N + K - 1)\exp(-\frac{1}{2}\frac{\Delta^2_{\min}T}{N\log N }).

results.notes: Conditional error probability; paper's K renamed K_c.

bound.regime: conditioned on change after round r*

symbols.K_c: rank of the beam that undergoes the change
symbols.T_1: E[r_c - r*, r* <= r_c <= log N], term depending on the change-time distribution

conditions: single abrupt change in the K_c-th best beam

source.label: lem:lc
source.quote: If the change occurs after the first \log \frac{N}{2K} rounds, the probability that the best arm is eliminated is upper bounded as P^{SH}_C(T | r_c > r^*) \leq \mathcal{T}_1(r_c) + 2\log 2NK \exp(-\frac{1}{2} \Delta_{\min}^2 \frac{T}{N \log N}).

symbols.K_c: rank of the beam that undergoes the change
symbols.T_1: E[r_c - r*, r* <= r_c <= log N], depends on the distribution of the change round

conditions: single abrupt change in the mean of the K_c-th best beam at 0 <= t_c <= T, making it optimal

source.quote: In case of a single abrupt change in the mean power of f_K at time 0 \leq t_c \leq T, the bound on the beam selection error is given by ... \leq \mathcal{T}_1(r_c) + 2 (2\log N + K - 1)\exp(-\frac{1}{2}\frac{\Delta^2_{\min}T}{N\log N }).

results.notes: Not exponentially small in general due to T_1 term. Logs base 2.

symbols.K_c: maximum index of the beam that can undergo a change (known to K-SHES)
symbols.Phi_F: sum_{i=1}^{K_c-1} [1 - F_{t_c}(t_i|r*)(1 - exp(-Delta_min^2/(2 N log N sigma_max^2)))], depends on change-time distribution

conditions: single abrupt change restricted to the top K_c beams
tuning: sequential halving until 2K_c beams remain, then equal allocation
results.notes: Paper's K renamed K_c; logs base 2.

bound.regime: change occurs in the first T[log(N/2K)/log N (1 - 1/(2K)) + 1/(2K)] slots with probability 1

symbols.K_c: maximum index of the beam that can undergo a change (known to K-SHES)

conditions: single abrupt change restricted to the top K_c beams
change occurs in the first T[log(K/2K_c)/log K (1 - 1/(2K_c)) + 1/(2K_c)] slots with probability 1
tuning: sequential halving until 2K_c beams remain, then equal allocation

source.quote: If the change occurs in the first T[\frac{\log(N/2K)}{\log N}(1 - \frac{1}{2K}) + \frac{1}{2K}] time slots with probability 1, then the beam selection error is exponentially bounded as P^{K-SHES}_C(T) \leq 2(2\log N + 2K - 1) \exp(-\frac{1}{2}\frac{\Delta^2_{min}T}{2N\log N \sigma^2_{\max}})

results.notes: Logs base 2; paper's K renamed K_c.
